In the past few decades, some but not all observational studies have found that vegetarians are healthier or live longer than
nonvegetarians. While some of the differences, such as those in lung cancer, are likely due largely to the lesser use of tobacco among
vegetarians, other differences favoring lower prevalence of disease may be attributable to the diet itself. Since those dietary factors or
other differences between vegetarians and nonvegetarians inﬂuence disease risk they, rather than solely the use or nonuse of animal
foods, are potentially responsible for some of the positive health effects (Mihrshai et al., 2017; Palacios and Maki, 2019). Therefore,
